knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5)
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(rxode2)

library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Thomaseth_1998_tcdd"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Thomaseth_1998_tcdd"))$description`
* Article: [Environ Health Perspect 1998;106(Suppl 2):743-753](https://doi.org/10.1289/ehp.98106743)

This is a *minimal physiologic toxicokinetic* (MPTK) model: a single whole-body
2,3,7,8-tetrachlorodibenzo-p-dioxin (TCDD) burden compartment whose distribution
volume is the body's total lipid mass. TCDD is eliminated by hepatic degradation
at a rate proportional to the fraction of body lipid held in the liver, so the
apparent elimination half-life is a function of body composition and changes as
the subject's body-mass index (BMI) changes with age. The model has no classical
dose events; it is run forward from an assumed serum level under a constant daily
intake.

# Population

Kinetic parameters -- the hepatic elimination rate `kf` and the background daily
intake `input` -- were estimated from repeated serum-dioxin measurements in
Operation Ranch Hand (RH) Vietnam veterans: 277 exposed veterans with three
samples (1982/1987/1992), plus additional RH and unexposed reference-group
observations (Table 1 of the source). The occupational-exposure parameter was
then estimated by linear regression on a subcohort of 253 male National Institute
for Occupational Safety and Health (NIOSH) chemical-plant workers who each had a
single serum-TCDD measurement (Table 2); the full NIOSH cohort is 5172 male
workers at 12 US plants. All subjects were adult males.

The population metadata are available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Thomaseth_1998_tcdd")()$population`.

# Source trace

The per-parameter origin is recorded as an in-file comment next to each `ini()`
entry in `inst/modeldb/specificDrugs/Thomaseth_1998_tcdd.R`. The table collects
them in one place. The lead on-disk source is a page-image scan of the article;
values are cited to their tables/figures within it.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `tkf` (kf)           | 0.02199 /day | Table 4, "NCME and log transformation" row (95% CI 0.020-0.024) |
| `input` (background) | 0.1251 pg/kg/day | Table 4, same row (95% CI 0.071-0.179); NIOSH scenario re-fit to 0.293 (Table 6) |
| `exposure` (occupational) | 0 (default) | Table 6 NIOSH estimate 232.7 pg/kg/day (95% CI 192-273); off by default |
| `alphaBMI`           | -3.755e-3 kg/m^2/year^2 | Figure 3 text (+/- 0.9e-3 SE) |
| `betaBMI`            | 0.26907 kg/m^2/year | Figure 3 text (+/- 0.04 SE) |
| `kadipose1`, `kadipose0` | 0.01264, 0.13305 | page 746, v_adipose = 1000*(0.01264*BMI - 0.13305); Knapik 1983 |
| `fliverlean`         | 0.0311 | page 745, liver = 3.11% of lean body mass (ICRP) |
| `flipadipose`, `flipliver`, `flipother` | 0.8, 0.069, 0.022 | page 745, lipid fractions of adipose / liver / other |
| `ladj0`              | 7 ppt | page 745/749, initial serum level fixed to 7 ppt |
| `etakf` (BSV on kf)  | 2.9e-5 (variance) | Table 4 footnote, additive on kf (Eq 18) |
| `propSd`             | 0.259 | Table 4 footnote, sigma2_eps = 0.0671 on log scale; sqrt = 0.259 (25.9% CV) |
| `d/dt(tcdd)`         | n/a | Equation 1 |
| `tcdd(0)`            | n/a | Equation 2 |
| `ladj = tcdd/TLV`    | n/a | Equation 3 |

## Dimensional analysis

Mechanistic models mix per-kg volumes, amounts and fractional rates, so each ODE
term is checked for unit consistency.

| Term | Units multiply out to |
|------|-----------------------|
| `kf * (lvliver/tlv) * tcdd` | (1/day) * (g/kg / g/kg) * pg = pg/day |
| `(input + exposure) * bw`   | (pg/kg/day) * kg = pg/day |
| `d/dt(tcdd)`                | pg/day |
| `TLV = tlv * bw`            | (g/kg) * kg = g |
| `ladj = tcdd / TLV`         | pg / g = ppt |
| `tcdd(0) = ladj0 * tlv0 * bw0` | (pg/g) * (g/kg) * kg = pg |

Every term is consistent. The liver-to-total lipid ratio `lvliver/tlv` is
dimensionless, so the hepatic elimination rate depends on body composition but
not on absolute body size; body weight enters only through the intake term.

# Validation

Because the model has no dose-concentration-time profile to integrate,
non-compartmental analysis (PKNCA) is not the right validation target. The
published results that pin the translation are the apparent elimination
half-lives at fixed body weights (Table 7), the lipid distribution across
compartments (Table 3), and the serum decay curves of Figure 6.

```{r mod}
mod <- rxode2::zeroRe(readModelDb("Thomaseth_1998_tcdd"))
```

## Apparent half-life vs. body weight (Table 7)

With a constant body weight and no intake, the burden decays mono-exponentially
at rate `kf * lvliver/tlv`. The implied half-life is read back from a
log-linear fit and compared against the paper's own Table 7 ("Thomaseth and
Salvan, this study") column, computed at a body height of 170 cm.

```{r halflife}
apparent_halflife <- function(bw_kg, ht_cm = 170) {
  bmi <- bw_kg / (ht_cm / 100)^2
  ev <- rxode2::et(seq(0, 20 * 365.25, length.out = 400))
  s <- rxode2::rxSolve(
    mod, ev,
    # constant body weight (no BMI drift) and no intake -> pure decay
    params = c(alphaBMI = 0, betaBMI = 0, input = 0, exposure = 0,
               BMI = bmi, HT = ht_cm, AGE_BASE = 40)
  )
  idx <- (nrow(s) %/% 2):nrow(s)
  slope <- coef(lm(log(s$ladj[idx]) ~ s$time[idx]))[2]
  (log(2) / -slope) / 365.25
}

halflife_tab <- tibble::tibble(
  bw_kg = c(70, 80, 90),
  simulated = vapply(bw_kg, apparent_halflife, numeric(1)),
  published = c(7.68, 9.85, 12.3) # Table 7, Thomaseth & Salvan column
)
halflife_tab |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (simulated - published) / published) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Body weight (kg)" = bw_kg,
    "Simulated t1/2 (yr)" = simulated,
    "Published t1/2 (yr)" = published,
    "Difference (%)" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Apparent TCDD half-life by body weight (height 170 cm).")

# Deterministic structural check: the solve reproduces the published half-lives
# essentially exactly (difference is numerical, not stochastic), so a tight
# bound is appropriate here.
stopifnot(all(abs(halflife_tab$simulated - halflife_tab$published) < 0.1))
```

## Lipid distribution across compartments (Table 3)

The fraction of total body lipid held in adipose, liver and other tissue at
body weight 70 kg / height 170 cm is compared against Table 3.

```{r lipiddist}
lipid_fractions <- function(bw_kg, ht_cm = 170) {
  bmi <- bw_kg / (ht_cm / 100)^2
  vadipose <- 1000 * (0.01264 * bmi - 0.13305)
  vliver <- 0.0311 * (1000 - vadipose)
  vother <- 1000 - vadipose - vliver
  lv <- c(adipose = 0.8 * vadipose, liver = 0.069 * vliver, other = 0.022 * vother)
  100 * lv / sum(lv)
}
dist70 <- lipid_fractions(70)
tibble::tibble(
  Compartment = c("Adipose", "Liver", "Other"),
  Simulated = unname(dist70),
  Published = c(87.7, 1.1, 11.2) # Table 3, 70 kg / 170 cm
) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Percent of total body lipid by compartment (70 kg, 170 cm).")

stopifnot(max(abs(dist70 - c(87.7, 1.1, 11.2))) < 0.15)
```

## Serum TCDD decay with changing body weight (Figure 6)

Figure 6 shows TCDD serum decay (intake off) from an initial level, for a
subject whose body weight stays constant or changes linearly over 20 years. A
linear body-weight change is produced here by a linear BMI drift
(`alphaBMI = 0`, `betaBMI` = the required slope).

```{r figure-6}
decay_scenario <- function(bw0, bw_final, ht_cm = 170, years = 20, ladj_start = 100) {
  bmi0 <- bw0 / (ht_cm / 100)^2
  bmi_final <- bw_final / (ht_cm / 100)^2
  beta <- (bmi_final - bmi0) / years # linear BMI drift (kg/m^2/year)
  ev <- rxode2::et(seq(0, years * 365.25, length.out = 200))
  s <- rxode2::rxSolve(
    mod, ev,
    params = c(alphaBMI = 0, betaBMI = beta, input = 0, exposure = 0,
               ladj0 = ladj_start, BMI = bmi0, HT = ht_cm, AGE_BASE = 40)
  )
  dplyr::tibble(year = s$time / 365.25, ladj = s$ladj,
                scenario = sprintf("%d -> %d kg", bw0, bw_final))
}

fig6 <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  decay_scenario(70, 70), decay_scenario(70, 60), decay_scenario(70, 80),
  decay_scenario(90, 90), decay_scenario(90, 60), decay_scenario(90, 100)
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(panel = ifelse(grepl("^70", scenario), "A: initial 70 kg", "B: initial 90 kg"))

ggplot(fig6, aes(year, ladj, colour = scenario)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~panel) +
  labs(x = "Years", y = "Serum TCDD (ppt, lipid-adjusted)",
       colour = "Body weight",
       title = "Figure 6 - serum TCDD decay under changing body weight",
       caption = "Replicates Figure 6 of Thomaseth & Salvan 1998 (intake off).") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

The constant-weight curves have the Table 7 half-lives; weight change that
*raises* body fat lengthens the apparent half-life (larger lipid distribution
volume), reproducing the qualitative behaviour discussed on page 751.

## Background and occupational intake

The model is driven forward by a constant daily intake proportional to body
weight. With background intake only (`input = 0.1251`, `exposure = 0`) the serum
level relaxes toward a low steady state; adding the fitted NIOSH occupational
intake (`exposure = 232.7`, with background re-fit to `input = 0.293`) drives it
far higher. A small cohort illustrates the between-subject spread from the
additive variability on `kf`.

```{r intake}
set.seed(1998)
n <- 100 # <= 200 per arm
cohort <- data.frame(
  id = seq_len(n),
  BMI = rnorm(n, 24.6, 3.1), # NIOSH at hire (Table 2)
  HT = 170,
  AGE_BASE = rnorm(n, 28.5, 7.6) # NIOSH at hire (Table 2)
)
ev <- rxode2::et(seq(0, 30 * 365.25, length.out = 120)) |>
  rxode2::et(id = seq_len(n))
ev <- merge(as.data.frame(ev), cohort, by = "id")

sim_bkg <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  readModelDb("Thomaseth_1998_tcdd"), ev,
  params = c(input = 0.1251, exposure = 0)
)
sim_occ <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  readModelDb("Thomaseth_1998_tcdd"), ev,
  params = c(input = 0.293, exposure = 232.7)
)

summ <- function(s, lab) {
  as.data.frame(s) |>
    dplyr::group_by(time) |>
    dplyr::summarise(med = median(ladj), lo = quantile(ladj, 0.1),
                     hi = quantile(ladj, 0.9), .groups = "drop") |>
    dplyr::mutate(scenario = lab, year = time / 365.25)
}
dplyr::bind_rows(summ(sim_bkg, "background only"),
                 summ(sim_occ, "NIOSH occupational")) |>
  ggplot(aes(year, med, colour = scenario, fill = scenario)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), alpha = 0.2, colour = NA) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Years", y = "Serum TCDD (ppt, lipid-adjusted)",
       title = "Background vs. occupational TCDD intake",
       caption = "Median with 10th-90th percentile band (n = 100).") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

The background-only steady state sits near the ~7 ppt level the authors assumed
for unexposed subjects, while continuous occupational intake accumulates to the
hundreds-of-ppt range reported for exposed NIOSH workers.

# Assumptions and deviations

- The lead on-disk source is a page-image scan of the 1998 article; the
  machine-readable full text was abstract-only. Every parameter was transcribed
  from the scanned tables and figure text (cited in the source-trace table) and
  cross-checked against the abstract, which quotes `kf = 0.022 /day` and
  `input = 0.1251 pg/kg/day`.
- Between-subject variability on `kf` is modelled as **additive** normal
  (`kf(i) = kf + e_kf`, Equation 18), not log-normal, reproducing the paper.
  With the published variance (SD ~0.0054, ~24% of `kf`) a sampled `kf` is
  positive well beyond the plausible range; the model does not enforce
  positivity, matching the source.
- The residual error is additive on the log-transformed concentration
  (Equation 19, `sigma2_eps = 0.0671`), encoded as proportional error
  (`propSd = sqrt(0.0671) = 0.259`) in linear space.
- `exposure` (occupational intake) defaults to 0 so the shipped model is a
  background individual. The fitted NIOSH occupational value (232.7 pg/kg/day,
  Table 6) and its paired background (0.293 pg/kg/day, re-fit to hold a 7 ppt
  baseline) are supplied as a scenario above. Intake is treated as constant;
  a time-limited work history can be reproduced by solving the exposed and
  unexposed periods piecewise.
- The population BMI age-drift sub-model (Equations 20-21) is the authors'
  NIOSH-subcohort fit; it is switched off (`alphaBMI = betaBMI = 0`) for the
  constant-body-weight checks that reproduce Table 3 and Table 7.
- Body height is held constant over the adult follow-up, the explicit
  simplifying assumption of the reformulated model (page 746).
- No correction notice for this article was found as of 2026-11-18.
```
